nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Eu precursor
nodes.procedure: Eu³⁺ is deposited onto the FeNi₂S₄ substrate under a reducing potential and in an OH⁻ environment, subsequently forming the Eu-OH-FeNi₂S₄ precursor.
nodes.source_text: followed by reduction of a layer of Eu to the surface through an electric field, resulting in the formation of the precursor. In the electrochemical deposition process... Eu³⁺ is deposited onto the FeNi₂S₄ substrate under a reducing potential and in an OH⁻ environment...

nodes.name: Argon-protected calcination
nodes.procedure: The Eu-OH-FeNi₂S₄ precursor was subjected to calcination under argon protection to obtain Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄. The inert gas argon ensures that FeNi₂S₄ was not oxidized to form oxides. Meanwhile, the oxygen affinity of the rare earth Eu guarantees that it would not be sulfided at the controlled temperature in the absence of a strong sulfur source.
nodes.source_text: The precursor was then subjected to calcination under argon protection to obtain Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄. In the subsequent argon atmosphere for the phase formation of Eu₂O₃...

nodes.description: LSV OER performance in 1 M KOH seawater (three-electrode, iR corrected)
nodes.source_text: The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) shown in Figure 3a demonstrates that Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ performs best in the potential range of 1.0-2.0 V in seawater... Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ exhibits superior anodic catalytic activity, with a current density of 1.43 V at 10 mA cm⁻² and 1.79 V at 100 mA cm⁻²... long-term stability assessment depicted in Figure 3d over a duration of 1000 h at a current density of 500 mA cm⁻² further confirms the excellent activity and stability of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ with iR correction.

nodes.description: Seawater electrolysis stability at 500 mA cm⁻²
nodes.source_text: In a kilowatt-level ASWE consisting of 17 small chambers, a traditional Ni mesh anode was used for electrolysis... After being subjected to a current density of 500 mA cm⁻², the flow channel of the anode plate underwent irreversible corrosion

nodes.description: kW-level ASWE with NiS₂ cathode - industrial conditions
nodes.source_text: The overall performance of seawater decomposition was evaluated in a customized large-scale corrosion-resistant commercial electrolysis device (electrode area: 1081.5 cm²)... Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ and NiS₂ were utilized as anodes and cathodes... at 80°C and with a 30% KOH solution... successfully met the industrial criterion of 1 A cm⁻² at a single cell voltage of 2.17 V... actual chamber voltage without iR correction was measured at 1.94 V, with fluctuations of less than 10% after continuous operation for over 100 h

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH seawater

nodes.description: Faradaic efficiency measurement in two-electrode setup
nodes.source_text: We employed Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ as the anode catalyst and Pt/C as the cathode catalyst to conduct a 1 h water electrolysis reaction at a current density of 30 mA/cm²... The calculated Faradaic efficiencies reached 94.75% for the anodic OER and 98.4% for the cathodic HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD analysis confirmed pure phase characteristics of FeNi₂S₄ consistent with JCPDS 47-1740 pattern for both Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ and FeNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray powder diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed that the obtained main structure exhibited pure phase characteristics of FeNi₂S₄, consistent with the JCPDS 47-1740 pattern (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: XAS of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄, FeNi₂S₄, and FeNi₂O₄ shows introduction of Eu₂O₃ led to decrease in Ni valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XAS of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄, FeNi₂S₄, FeNi₂S₄, and FeNi₂O₄. X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) spectrum demonstrated that introduction of Eu₂O₃ led to a decrease in Ni valence state for charge conservation purposes (Figure 1h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and corresponding EDS elemental mapping verified formation of Eu₂O₃ loaded on FeNi₂S₄ with distinct elemental distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High angle dark field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and corresponding EDS elemental mapping further verified its formation of Eu₂O₃ loaded and element composition.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy showed carbon vibration positions and catalyst signals on carbon fiber substrate for Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy and its optical imaging are displayed on a carbon fiber substrate, where the target sample is grown around each carbon fiber.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms existence of Eu and O elements in Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄; peak splitting shows increasing low valence states of Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The full spectrum of XPS also confirms the existence of the Eu and O elements. This facilitated oxidation and active species formation during the oxidation process, which is consistent with the phenomenon of increasing low valence states of Ni obtained by peak splitting in XPS (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM characterized the morphology of the Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ nanomaterial structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was used to characterize the morphology of the nanomaterial structure (Figure S8).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS displays elemental compositions of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ and FeNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) further displays the elemental compositions of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ and FeNi₂S₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM proves presence of Eu₂O₃ and FeNi₂S₄ phases through lattice stripe width measurement corresponding to crystal planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ can also prove the presence of Eu₂O₃ and FeNi₂S₄ phases (Figures S16 and S17).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS clearly distinguishes existence of Fe, Ni, and Eu in Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Further, EELS of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ can clearly distinguish the existence of Fe, Ni, and Eu (Figure S10).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ fluorescence spectra under MQAE labeling show higher Cl⁻ concentration near Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ surface at 2.0 V indicating inhibition of Cl⁻ adsorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the fluorescence intensity at a chlorine oxidation potential of 2.0 V, it was observed that the concentration of Cl⁻ in the Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ solution was higher.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman confirms structural stability with Fe-S and Ni-S vibrations unchanged; peak near 700 cm⁻¹ shifts to higher Raman shift with potential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, structural stability during the catalytic processes was confirmed through in situ Raman spectroscopy (Figure S23).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-FTIR shows OH⁻ at 3400 cm⁻¹ with Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄ exhibiting stronger OH⁻ adsorption compared to FeNi₂S₄.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The in situ ATR-FTIR of Eu₂O₃/FeNi₂S₄, FeNi₂S₄ and Eu₂O₃ in seawater is shown in Figure S26, with OH⁻ located at 3400 cm⁻¹.
